q-124179.worked_solution:
Let $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}$ be a piecewise smooth path in the $xy$-plane, and let $-C$ be the curve consisting of the same points as $C$ but with the opposite orientation. 

For line integrals with respect to $y,$ we have the following properties:

- ${\int }_{-C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y=-{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

- ${\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y & ={\int }_{{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{-{C}_{1}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{{C}_{2}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-3+5 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

q-124347.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14226618/assets/0361756c09e5f72ddb040240bbec492c0a9dd3562307253ae31bece95bb41d88.png)

Calculate ${∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y,$  where $C={C}_{1}\cup {C}_{2}\cup {C}_{3}$ is the path comprising of two line segments and a semicircle or radius $4,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, as shown above.
q-124347.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to $y$ along a path $C$ is equal to the net change in $y$ between the terminal and initial points:

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y={y}_{2}-{y}_{1},
$$

where ${y}_{2}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the terminal point, and ${y}_{1}$ is the $y$-coordinate of the initial point.

In our case, the initial and terminal points are the same (since the path is closed and is traversed only once). Therefore, ${y}_{1}={y}_{2},$ and we have

$$
{∮}_{C}\,\text{d}y=0.
$$
